## Source context

-Built for trackstar customer Leftfield Group (requested via the cin7 channel), Linear TRA-1900. Multi-tenant WMS; base URL is per-tenant by subdomain. Characterized against the writes-safe, vendor-owned sandbox mirror (subdomain `tcd`). Scope: reads — inventory, inventory_ledger, products, warehouses, warehouse_locations, warehouse_customers, inbound_shipments, orders; writes — create/update inbound_shipment, create/update/cancel order.

+Built for customer Leftfield Group (requested via the cin7 channel), Linear TRA-1900. Multi-tenant WMS, base URL per tenant subdomain. Characterized against the writes-safe, vendor-owned sandbox mirror (subdomain `tcd`).
## Auth shape

-- **Custom session-token header, exchanged at install.** `POST /users/sign_in` (no auth header) with `{"user":{"email","password"}}` → body containing `token`. Every later call sends `Authorization: Token token="<token>", email="<email>"` — literal `Token` keyword, both values double-quoted, email in the header. Not Bearer; build the string explicitly. `get_integration_secret` does the exchange and stores `{email, password, token, subdomain, sandbox}`; `validate_integration_secret` is a `pass` (auth already verified by the successful sign_in).

-- **No refresh endpoint.** No documented TTL; "one concurrent login per account" (a browser login invalidates the API token). A stale token surfaces as 401 → `clarus_request` re-calls sign_in once, updates the secret (when `connection_id` set), retries. Every auth call passes `ignore_log=True` (creds + token in body).

-- **Base URL** from stored subdomain + sandbox flag: sandbox `https://{subdomain}.api.clarus-mirror.co.uk`, prod `https://{subdomain}.api.clarus.co.uk` (prod TLD unconfirmed — see Sandbox vs. production divergence).

-- **Transport: hybrid.** Reads are GraphQL (`POST /graphql`, Relay connections). Writes are REST JSON:API (`POST/PUT/PATCH /api/...`, body wrapped in `{"data":{"attributes":{...}, "relationships":{...}}}`, line collections under `lines_changes:[{type:"ADD"|"UPDATE", attributes:{...}}]`). One shared `clarus_request` helper serves both.

-- **Pagination: Relay cursor.** `all(first:N, after:"<cursor>")` → `{pageInfo{endCursor hasNextPage}, edges{node{...}}}`. `next_token = endCursor` while `hasNextPage`, else `None`; terminate on `hasNextPage == false`, not on `meta.total_records`. Exceptions: `stock_balances::all` accepts no `after`/`first`/date filter → full scan; `warehouses::all` returns all rows, no pageInfo; `shipments::all` exposes no `first`/`after` (filtered by `reference`). Empty windows are clean (`hasNextPage:false, edges:[]` — no 404, no ghost pages). `<resource>::all` accepts a `reference:` filter (used for write read-back) and stocks accepts `product_code:`, but a `filters:` arg is rejected.

-- **Connection accessor quirk:** `stock_balances::all` and `warehouses::all` require a `nodes` sub-selection (`all { nodes { ... } }`); direct field access fails with `Field 'x' doesn't exist on type 'XxxConnection'`. The `edges{node}` shape works on the paginated connections.

## Known quirks / unknowns

-- **SKU (`code`) is NOT unique.** Distinct product ids share a `code`, differing only by `description` (e.g. code "40113" → product ids 108/145/146). The internal `product.id` is the identity everywhere; `code` is carried as the separate `sku` field. Posting `code` where Clarus expects an internal id would 422 or silently mismatch.

-- **Order `warehouse_id` is frequently null** (~14/25 live orders). No line-level warehouse source exists. The canonical field is `allow_not_implemented`, so `format_order` emits `None` when null — no fabrication.

-- **Country codes are Clarus-specific, not ISO 3166 alpha-2.** Live addresses use `"GB-UKM"` (sometimes plain `"GB"`). Read passes through as-is; the write schema keeps the default lenient `Length(min=2, max=10)` (a `Length(equal=2)` would reject `"GB-UKM"`).

-- **No pricing anywhere.** `goods_outs`/`goods_out_lines`/products expose no price/tax/discount/total/currency on read OR write, so those fields → `IntegrationNotImplemented`. Exception: `invoice_currency_code` is a hardcoded `"GBP"` (required non-nullable field; Clarus is a UK-based WMS).

-- **Lot/batch lives on `string1`** (custom-field slot; lines expose `string1..5`, `datetime1..5`, etc.). Round-trips on receipt lines and order lines. But `stocks.string1` is not seedable via API (putaway is UI-only), so `inventory.lots` is built spec-only and unvalidated live. `stringN` is per-account configurable via `account.use_stringN` — the exact slot could differ per tenant.

## Field-mapping decisions
-- `create_order_shipment` — verify-after-write (2026-05-20)
-  - Decision: after the `POST`, re-`GET` the fulfillment list and confirm a
-    fulfillmentId not present before the POST appeared; raise a loud
-    `PokedexException` (400, `origin="integration"`) if none did. The message
-    is generic ("did not land … retry / escalate"), but when `shipped_date`
-    parses to earlier than the order's `creationDate` it names that as the
-    cause — eBay's confirmed discard trigger.
-  - Reason: eBay's `201` is unreliable (see "Known quirks"). Without the check,
-    `create_order_shipment` returned a misleading `200` to the customer with an
-    empty `shipments` list and `status: open`. The request is not pre-screened
-    against our own logic — eBay's discard is the trigger; we only surface it
-    accurately.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — Datadog traces `4761577796659203049` et al.;
-    direct read-only `GET`s against eBay 26h later confirmed the fulfillment
-    never existed; controlled re-post on 2026-05-20 reproduced the discard and
-    the new check raised the loud `400` as designed.
-- `create_order_shipment` — order re-fetched after the POST (2026-05-20)
-  - Decision: the order is fetched once before the POST (to map SKU →
-    `lineItemId`) and again after, and `format_order` is given the post-POST
-    snapshot.
-  - Reason: the prior code formatted the response from the pre-POST order, so
-    `status` was always the stale pre-fulfillment value (`open`) and the
-    response failed the `status ∈ {partially_fulfilled, fulfilled}` validator
-    even on the success path.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
-- `get_products` / `adjust_inventory` — SKU percent-encoded in the
-  `getInventoryItem` path (2026-07-27)
-  - Decision: `quote(sku, safe="")` at every
-    `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` interpolation.
-  - Reason: `/` splits the SKU into extra path segments and `#` truncates it at
-    a fragment, so eBay receives a different resource id than intended and
-    returns `404`. `requests` does not encode either character.
-  - Evidence: `get_products` on connection
-    `5238ee309955435bb6f64bb5bc883e97` failed every hourly crawl from
-    2026-07-27T08:22Z with `errorId 25710` at the single-item fetch; the same
-    4 SKUs all returned `200` with the encoded segment, and the full prod
-    dry-run crawl then completed with 382 items.

## Auth shape

- **v4 OAuth2 password grant, one token drives both API families.** Exchange: `POST https://atlas{-sandbox}.jooraccess.com/auth/` with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `username`, `password`, `grant_type=password` — **multipart form parts only**, not JSON or urlencoded. Access token lives 10h. Refresh at the same endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`; the response advertises a 7776000s refresh token but JOOR's docs say 86400s and in practice an expired refresh can come back 400 rather than 401, so `joor_request` retries the full password grant on any refresh failure.

-- **Authorization header: the bare token, no `Bearer ` prefix**, sent unchanged on v2 and v4 paths (verified: v4 accepts bare or `Bearer `, v2 bare or `OAuth2 <token>` — no separate v2 token needed).

- **Every v4 path needs an `account` query param** (the numeric JOOR account id). No endpoint discovers it, so it's a manifest input.

- **Expired-token signaling differs by version**: v2 is a plain 401; v4 answers 200 or 400 with `errors[0].status == "AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED"`. `joor_request` watches both, refreshes once, then raises invalid credentials.

-- **Auth failure classification**: 401 OR body `error` of `invalid_client`/`invalid_grant` → invalid credentials (JOOR reports a rejected client in the body; `invalid_grant` is RFC 6749's code for a bad password or spent refresh token). -## API Characteristics
-- Transport: REST / JSON. Base URL `https://app.orderdesk.me/api/v2` (constant, not tenant-specific).

-- Auth: two static request headers — `ORDERDESK-STORE-ID` and `ORDERDESK-API-KEY`. No token exchange, no refresh. `get_integration_secret` stores `{store_id, api_key}` verbatim; `validate_integration_secret` should hit `GET /test` (returns `{"status":"success","message":"Connection Successful"}`) or `GET /store` for the live round-trip. `me`/`safe_me`/`safe_integration_secret_keys` expose `store_id` only — never `api_key`.

-- Pagination: offset + limit. Orders `limit` max **500** (values >500 are silently reduced, so compare `records_returned` to the requested limit — don't assume you got 500). Envelope: `{status, execution_time, total_records, records_returned, offset, limit, <collection>}`. Terminate when `records_returned < requested limit`. Same shape on `/inventory-items` (there `total_records`/`limit`/`offset` come back as JSON strings, not ints).

-- Empty-window behavior (list endpoints, verified live): pagination metadata is computed **post-filter** — folder-filtered `total_records` was 284,717 vs 1,789,621 unfiltered, and a far-future `modified_start_date` returned `total_records: 0`. An empty window returns a clean **HTTP 200** with `total_records: 0, records_returned: 0` and the collection key **present as an empty array `[]`** (not omitted). No 404 on empty. Consequence: terminate on `records_returned`, and index the collection key directly (error-driven, no defensive `.get()`). (Corrected during fan-out: the captured `samples/orders_empty_window.json` and a live far-future-window crawl both show `"orders": []` present; the earlier "omits the key" wording was wrong.)
-- Response format: JSON. Every response carries `{status: "success"|"error", execution_time}`. Errors return an HTTP 4xx plus `{"status":"error","message":"Invalid Route"}` (bad path) etc.
-- Token refresh: static creds, no refresh.

-- Webhooks: none in scope. No webhook endpoint in the v2 API reference or `llms.txt`. OrderDesk has UI-configured store "rules/triggers" that can notify a URL, but no documented HMAC-signed push. unknown — verify during implementation if push is ever wanted.

-- Rate limit: token bucket, refills ~3 req/s with a 20-request burst (~100 requests over a rolling 30s window). Over-limit returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests** with header **`X-Retry-After`** (seconds to wait) — note the **non-standard header name** (`X-Retry-After`, not `Retry-After`).

-- Idempotency: no documented idempotency key on writes. Re-posting `POST /orders/{id}/shipments` creates a duplicate shipment record (shipments have no natural key). Flag for the shipment write path.

-- Warehouse availability (cart): **none**. No `/warehouses`, `/locations`, `/facilities`, or `/fulfillment-providers` endpoint (all return 404 Invalid Route). Inventory items carry a single `location` string (empty in sandbox) and store setting `multi_location_inventory` is off → one implicit location. `order_metadata.fulfillment_center` (e.g. `"SF-YOR"`) is a per-order warehouse-code hint but is store-specific metadata, not an enumerable warehouse list. `get_warehouses` is not implementable — omit the method (don't ship the scaffolded raise-only stub).

## Field-mapping decisions
-- **`create_order_shipment` verifies after write.** It snapshots fulfillment ids before the POST, re-`GET`s
-  after, and raises a `400` `PokedexException` (`origin="integration"`) if no new id appeared; the message
-  names the shipped-before-created cause when `shipped_date < creationDate`. Why: the `201` is unreliable, and
-  without the check the customer got a misleading `200` with no shipment. We surface eBay's discard, we don't
-  pre-screen the request. Evidence: Pylon #4422, Datadog trace `4761577796659203049`; the 2026-05-20 re-post
-  reproduced the discard and the check raised.
-- **`create_order_shipment` formats the order re-fetched after the POST.** The pre-POST snapshot (used only for
-  SKU to `lineItemId`) has stale `status: open`, which failed the `partially_fulfilled | fulfilled` response
-  validator even on success. Evidence: Pylon #4422 `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
-- **SKU is `quote(sku, safe="")`-encoded at every `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` path**
-  (`get_products`, `adjust_inventory`). Why: see the `/` and `#` quirk. Evidence: connection
-  `5238ee30...` failed every hourly `get_products` crawl with `errorId 25710` until encoded; all 4 SKUs then
-  returned `200` and the prod dry-run crawl completed with 382 items.
+- `create_order_shipment` — verify-after-write (2026-05-20)
+  - Decision: after the `POST`, re-`GET` the fulfillment list and confirm a
+    fulfillmentId not present before the POST appeared; raise a loud
+    `PokedexException` (400, `origin="integration"`) if none did. The message
+    is generic ("did not land … retry / escalate"), but when `shipped_date`
+    parses to earlier than the order's `creationDate` it names that as the
+    cause — eBay's confirmed discard trigger.
+  - Reason: eBay's `201` is unreliable (see "Known quirks"). Without the check,
+    `create_order_shipment` returned a misleading `200` to the customer with an
+    empty `shipments` list and `status: open`. The request is not pre-screened
+    against our own logic — eBay's discard is the trigger; we only surface it
+    accurately.
+  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — Datadog traces `4761577796659203049` et al.;
+    direct read-only `GET`s against eBay 26h later confirmed the fulfillment
+    never existed; controlled re-post on 2026-05-20 reproduced the discard and
+    the new check raised the loud `400` as designed.
+- `create_order_shipment` — order re-fetched after the POST (2026-05-20)
+  - Decision: the order is fetched once before the POST (to map SKU →
+    `lineItemId`) and again after, and `format_order` is given the post-POST
+    snapshot.
+  - Reason: the prior code formatted the response from the pre-POST order, so
+    `status` was always the stale pre-fulfillment value (`open`) and the
+    response failed the `status ∈ {partially_fulfilled, fulfilled}` validator
+    even on the success path.
+  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
+- `get_products` / `adjust_inventory` — SKU percent-encoded in the
+  `getInventoryItem` path (2026-07-27)
+  - Decision: `quote(sku, safe="")` at every
+    `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` interpolation.
+  - Reason: `/` splits the SKU into extra path segments and `#` truncates it at

+    order can be mode=freight with needsTransportation=false. Quotes are deliberately
+    excluded: no schema query lists rate quotes, only an opaque `selectedShippingRateId`
+    (null on all sampled orders); the chosen carrier's actual cost already maps to
+    `packages[].shipping_cost` via `transportation.costInCents`.
+  - Evidence: live freight orders on the Rowlo LLC prod connection (e.g. order
+    `3005930639`, pallet 48x40x59 @ 855 lbs). `pallets` is null on parcel orders, hence
+    the `or []`.
- `format_inbound_shipment` — receipt line item `sku` from the source line item
-  - Decision: derived receipt line items emit `li["sku"]`, not `IntegrationNotImplemented`.
-  - Reason: receipts reloaded from `previous_receipts` carry a real sku, and the crawler's
-    `create_implemented_dict` requires uniform implementation across items, so the mix
-    crashed the inbound crawl (`Implemented dict conflict: sku ...`).
+  - Decision: emit `"sku": li["sku"]` on each derived receipt line item instead of
+    `IntegrationNotImplemented`. The receipt is built by iterating the inbound's own
+    `line_items`, each of which already carries the real sku.
+  - Reason: receipts reloaded from storage (`previous_receipts`) carry a real sku, so a
+    freshly-derived receipt emitting `IntegrationNotImplemented` makes
+    `receipts[].line_items[].sku` inconsistent across receipts in a batch. The crawler's
+    `create_implemented_dict` requires a field to be uniformly implemented (or not) across
+    all items, so the mix crashed the whole inbound crawl
+    (`Implemented dict conflict: sku is set to True but got value IntegrationNotImplemented`).
+  - Evidence: prod crawl error `get_inbound_shipments`; the sku was available all along on
+    the source line item, so this is faithful, not a synthesized value.
- `create_order` — set `packageItemsRequired: true`
-  - Decision: `build_common_order_attr_parts` (`queries.py`) adds it to
-    `orderAttributes` on both parcel and freight creates, forcing per-package item capture.
-  - Placement: it belongs on `orderAttributes`, not the top-level input; the top level
-    rejects it (`doesn't accept argument 'packageItemsRequired'`). Moselle sandbox order
-    `1318593841` accepted it without us sending packages.
-  - Reason: prevents the empty `packages[].items` state (Known quirks). Luminous (the OMS)
-    creates all of this customer's orders via `POST /wms/orders`, so it reaches them.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4273 (order `5609035497`, Wayfair) and #4561 (`6561807448`, Home
-    Depot EDI), both created without the flag and shipped with empty items.
+  - Decision: add `packageItemsRequired: true` inside `orderAttributes` in
+    `build_create_order_mutation` (`queries.py`), forcing Flowspace to record
+    per-package item contents at fulfillment.
+  - Placement: the field lives on `OutboundParcelOrderAttributes` (the type of
+    `orderAttributes`), **not** the top-level `CreateOutboundParcelOrderInput`.
+    Setting it at the input level is rejected with
+    `InputObject 'CreateOutboundParcelOrderInput' doesn't accept argument
+    'packageItemsRequired'`. Confirmed via schema introspection and a Moselle-sandbox
+    create test (order `1318593841`); the create is accepted without us sending any
+    packages/shipments.
+  - Reason: prevents the empty `packages[].items` state (see Known quirks) for all
+    future Trackstar-created orders. Luminous (the OMS) creates all of this customer's
+    orders via `POST /wms/orders`, so the directive reaches them.
+  - Evidence: Pylon #4273 (order `5609035497`, Wayfair) and #4561 (order `6561807448`,
+    Home Depot EDI). Datadog confirms both were created via our `createOutboundParcelOrder`
+    without the flag and later shipped with empty `packages[].items`.
- `format_order` — backfill shipment line items from order line items
-  - Decision: when `packages and status == "fulfilled"` but `shipment_line_items` is
-    empty, backfill from the order `line_items` (mirrors infoplus). Safe because
-    Flowspace emits one shipment per fully-shipped order.
-  - Reason: `packageItemsRequired` can't repair orders that already shipped empty or
-    orders created outside our API; resync repairs history.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4273, #4561; backfill yields `EC700356 ×1` for `6561807448`.
+  - Decision: when an order is fully shipped (`packages and status == "fulfilled"`) but
+    aggregated `shipment_line_items` is empty, backfill it from the order `line_items`
+    (mirrors `infoplus/integration.py:format_order`). Flowspace emits one shipment per
+    fully-shipped order, so this is safe at the shipment level.
+  - Reason: the source-side `packageItemsRequired` flag cannot retroactively repair
+    orders that already shipped empty, and does not cover any order created outside our
+    API. This read-side fallback repairs history (via resync) and is a safety net.
+  - Evidence: Pylon #4273, #4561 — same orders as above; verified the backfill populates
+    `EC700356 ×1` for `6561807448` and leaves normally-populated orders untouched.
# Integration Patterns — Operational Source of Truth
-> **Doctrine version:** 2.4 · last updated 2026-09-28 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.
+> **Doctrine version:** 2.3 · last updated 2026-09-22 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.

> Versioned **independently of the skills that consume it.** Changes to the rules below bump the doctrine version here — not `/plan-integration`'s. The skills point at this file; they don't own its history. (Pre-1.0 doctrine changes were tracked under `plan-integration` CHANGELOG entries 1.17–1.31, before the doctrine carried its own version.)

This file is the canonical pattern reference for integration subagents (`integration-api-validator`, `integration-function-writer`, `integration-reviewer`). Subagents start with clean context and **do not** auto-load the project CLAUDE.md, so this file duplicates the rules subagents need.

**Vendor variants that aren't a literal 403** still use the same shape. The trigger is "permission missing for this URL" — whether the signal is HTTP 403, HTTP 402 (payment required → billing tier doesn't include this), a JSON `errors[].message == "Access denied."` inside a 401, or text like `"AuthorizationException"` in the body. Detect the signal, then run the same record-and-raise.

-**Under the permission validator, one call per endpoint is proof of access.** Its gets run under a short time limit, so a `get_*` that walks a catalogue or makes a detail call per record branches on `self.in_perm_validator()` and requests a page size of 1: inline, no constant, no comment. A bigger "safe" page brings the timeout back as the account grows.
##### Reviewer enforcement (permission tracking)

- 403 (or vendor-equivalent permission signal) raises `create_invalid_credentials_exception` instead of `create_permissions_exception(path)` → `[BLOCK]`. The customer gets a "creds are bad" notification when the right remediation is "grant scope to this URL."

+    try:

+                return
+            leftover = [

+                for child in traces[trace_id].spans
+                if child is not request_span
+                and child.duration_ns is None
+                and child.span_type == SpanTypes.LLM
+                and _span_is_descendant_of(child, request_span)

import sys
from typing import Callable
from typing import Optional
from typing import Protocol
from typing import Union

from ddtrace._trace.provider import BaseContextProvider
from ddtrace._trace.span import Span
from ddtrace.internal import core
from ddtrace.internal._context_watcher import PYTHON_CONTEXT_SWITCH_EVENT
from ddtrace.internal._context_watcher import register_context_watcher
from ddtrace.internal.native._native import Context
from ddtrace.internal.settings._config import config


class TracerProtocol(Protocol):
    @property
    def context_provider(self) -> BaseContextProvider: ...


_ContextActivationListener = Callable[[BaseContextProvider, Optional[Union[Context, Span]]], None]
_ContextSwitchListener = Callable[[], None]
_ThreadContextListeners = tuple[_ContextActivationListener, _ContextSwitchListener]


if sys.platform == "linux":
    from ddtrace.internal.native._native import detach_otel_thread_context
    from ddtrace.internal.native._native import update_otel_thread_context_from_context
    from ddtrace.internal.native._native import update_otel_thread_context_from_span

    def register_otel_thread_context_listener(tracer: TracerProtocol) -> Optional[_ThreadContextListeners]:
        if not config._otel_thread_context_enabled:
            return None

        def _sync_otel_thread_context(ctx: Optional[Union[Context, Span]]) -> None:
            if type(ctx) is Span:
                sampling_priority = ctx._local_root.context.sampling_priority
                trace_flags = 1 if sampling_priority is not None and sampling_priority > 0 else 0
                update_otel_thread_context_from_span(ctx, trace_flags)
            elif isinstance(ctx, Context):
                sampling_priority = ctx.sampling_priority
                trace_flags = 1 if sampling_priority is not None and sampling_priority > 0 else 0
                update_otel_thread_context_from_context(ctx, trace_flags)
            else:
                detach_otel_thread_context()

        def _sync_active_otel_thread_context() -> None:
            _sync_otel_thread_context(tracer.context_provider.active())

        def _on_context_provider_activate(provider: BaseContextProvider, ctx: Optional[Union[Context, Span]]) -> None:
            if provider is tracer.context_provider:
                _sync_otel_thread_context(ctx)

        register_context_watcher()
        core.on("ddtrace.context_provider.activate", _on_context_provider_activate)
        core.on(PYTHON_CONTEXT_SWITCH_EVENT, _sync_active_otel_thread_context)
        return _on_context_provider_activate, _sync_active_otel_thread_context

else:

## Auth shape

-- **Custom session-token header, exchanged at install.** `POST /users/sign_in` (no auth header) with `{"user":{"email","password"}}` → body containing `token`. Every later call sends `Authorization: Token token="<token>", email="<email>"` — literal `Token` keyword, both values double-quoted, email in the header. Not Bearer; build the string explicitly. `get_integration_secret` does the exchange and stores `{email, password, token, subdomain, sandbox}`; `validate_integration_secret` is a `pass` (auth already verified by the successful sign_in).

## Known quirks / unknowns

-- **SKU (`code`) is NOT unique.** Distinct product ids share a `code`, differing only by `description` (e.g. code "40113" → product ids 108/145/146). The internal `product.id` is the identity everywhere; `code` is carried as the separate `sku` field. Posting `code` where Clarus expects an internal id would 422 or silently mismatch.

-- **Order `warehouse_id` is frequently null** (~14/25 live orders). No line-level warehouse source exists. The canonical field is `allow_not_implemented`, so `format_order` emits `None` when null — no fabrication.

-- **Country codes are Clarus-specific, not ISO 3166 alpha-2.** Live addresses use `"GB-UKM"` (sometimes plain `"GB"`). Read passes through as-is; the write schema keeps the default lenient `Length(min=2, max=10)` (a `Length(equal=2)` would reject `"GB-UKM"`).

-- **No pricing anywhere.** `goods_outs`/`goods_out_lines`/products expose no price/tax/discount/total/currency on read OR write, so those fields → `IntegrationNotImplemented`. Exception: `invoice_currency_code` is a hardcoded `"GBP"` (required non-nullable field; Clarus is a UK-based WMS).

-- **Lot/batch lives on `string1`** (custom-field slot; lines expose `string1..5`, `datetime1..5`, etc.). Round-trips on receipt lines and order lines. But `stocks.string1` is not seedable via API (putaway is UI-only), so `inventory.lots` is built spec-only and unvalidated live. `stringN` is per-account configurable via `account.use_stringN` — the exact slot could differ per tenant.

## Known quirks
-- **eBay returns `201` for `createShippingFulfillment` even when it silently
-  discards the fulfillment.** Observed in Pylon #4422: 5 POSTs across 2 orders
-  all got `201` + a `Location` header, but the fulfillment never persisted —
-  `GET .../shipping_fulfillment` returned `total: 0`, the order stayed
-  `NOT_STARTED`, and a `GET` on eBay's own `Location` URL returned
-  `400 Invalid Shipping Fulfillment Id`. The `201` cannot be trusted as proof
-  of success.
-- **Confirmed discard cause: `shippedDate` earlier than the order's
-  `creationDate`.** Both stuck orders sent a date-only ship date coerced to
-  `T07:00:00Z` (midnight US Pacific) that landed hours before the order was
-  created. Confirmed by a controlled test on 2026-05-20 against
-  `01-14673-89727`: re-posting with `shippedDate 2026-05-19T07:00:00Z` (before
-  the `2026-05-19T16:55:47Z` creationDate) got `201` + silent discard;
-  re-posting with `shippedDate` omitted (eBay stamps the call time) persisted
-  the fulfillment and moved the order to `FULFILLED`. Same for
-- **Seller SKUs are free-text and routinely contain URL-structural
-  characters.** On the prod catalog behind connection
-  `5238ee309955435bb6f64bb5bc883e97` (org `org_2UMFFPiFuhLxf6GBNVvINRBgYOm`),
-  160 SKUs reach the `getInventoryItem` single-item path and 4 of them carry
-  `LM-BK-38-100 / CT-4B`, `LM-BK-14-100 / CT-4B`. Any SKU interpolated into a
-  path must be percent-encoded — `requests` encodes spaces but leaves `/` and
-  `#` alone, so an unencoded SKU silently retargets the request and eBay
-  answers `404 errorId 25710 API_INVENTORY`. Verified 2026-07-27: all 4 SKUs
-  return the full inventory item once the segment is encoded.
-- **A `+` in the query string is a literal plus, not a space.**
-  `getOffers?sku=first+test+sku` (the default `requests` encoding) answers `404 errorId 25713 "This Offer is not available"`, while
-  `?sku=first%20test%20sku` returns offer `9493649010`. `ebay_request` encodes
-  every query with `quote` so spaces go as `%20`.
-- **`getShippingFulfillments` can repeat a line item reference.** Order `27-15088-15985` lists
-  `{"lineItemId": "10087743998327"}` four times in one fulfillment (the line is quantity 1, FULFILLED).
-  `format_order` skips exact repeats; a differing repeat still fails the duplicate check.
-- **`getShippingFulfillments` does not echo `shippingCarrierCode`.** A
-  fulfillment created with `shippingCarrierCode` set comes back from the `GET`
-  with no carrier field, so `format_order` maps `carrier_name` / `carrier_id`
-  to `None`. Pre-existing (see commit `379f4efb3`); the tracking number is
-  returned normally.

## Field-mapping decisions
-- `create_order_shipment` — verify-after-write (2026-05-20)
-  - Decision: after the `POST`, re-`GET` the fulfillment list and confirm a
-    fulfillmentId not present before the POST appeared; raise a loud
-    `PokedexException` (400, `origin="integration"`) if none did. The message
-    is generic ("did not land … retry / escalate"), but when `shipped_date`
-    parses to earlier than the order's `creationDate` it names that as the
-    cause — eBay's confirmed discard trigger.
-  - Reason: eBay's `201` is unreliable (see "Known quirks"). Without the check,
-    `create_order_shipment` returned a misleading `200` to the customer with an
-    empty `shipments` list and `status: open`. The request is not pre-screened
-    against our own logic — eBay's discard is the trigger; we only surface it
-    accurately.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — Datadog traces `4761577796659203049` et al.;
-    direct read-only `GET`s against eBay 26h later confirmed the fulfillment
-    never existed; controlled re-post on 2026-05-20 reproduced the discard and
-    the new check raised the loud `400` as designed.
-- `create_order_shipment` — order re-fetched after the POST (2026-05-20)
-  - Decision: the order is fetched once before the POST (to map SKU →
-    `lineItemId`) and again after, and `format_order` is given the post-POST
-    snapshot.
-  - Reason: the prior code formatted the response from the pre-POST order, so
-    `status` was always the stale pre-fulfillment value (`open`) and the
-    response failed the `status ∈ {partially_fulfilled, fulfilled}` validator
-    even on the success path.
-  - Evidence: Pylon #4422 — `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
-- `get_products` / `adjust_inventory` — SKU percent-encoded in the
-  `getInventoryItem` path (2026-07-27)
-  - Decision: `quote(sku, safe="")` at every
-    `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` interpolation.
-  - Reason: `/` splits the SKU into extra path segments and `#` truncates it at
-    a fragment, so eBay receives a different resource id than intended and
-    returns `404`. `requests` does not encode either character.
-  - Evidence: `get_products` on connection
-    `5238ee309955435bb6f64bb5bc883e97` failed every hourly crawl from
-    2026-07-27T08:22Z with `errorId 25710` at the single-item fetch; the same
-    4 SKUs all returned `200` with the encoded segment, and the full prod
-    dry-run crawl then completed with 382 items.
+- **`create_order_shipment` verifies after write.** It snapshots fulfillment ids before the POST, re-`GET`s
+  after, and raises a `400` `PokedexException` (`origin="integration"`) if no new id appeared; the message
+  names the shipped-before-created cause when `shipped_date < creationDate`. Why: the `201` is unreliable, and
+  without the check the customer got a misleading `200` with no shipment. We surface eBay's discard, we don't
+  pre-screen the request. Evidence: Pylon #4422, Datadog trace `4761577796659203049`; the 2026-05-20 re-post
+  reproduced the discard and the check raised.
+- **`create_order_shipment` formats the order re-fetched after the POST.** The pre-POST snapshot (used only for
+  SKU to `lineItemId`) has stale `status: open`, which failed the `partially_fulfilled | fulfilled` response
+  validator even on success. Evidence: Pylon #4422 `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
+- **SKU is `quote(sku, safe="")`-encoded at every `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` path**
+  (`get_products`, `adjust_inventory`). Why: see the `/` and `#` quirk. Evidence: connection
+  `5238ee30...` failed every hourly `get_products` crawl with `errorId 25710` until encoded; all 4 SKUs then
+  returned `200` and the prod dry-run crawl completed with 382 items.

## Known quirks
- **Empty `packages[].items` on shipped orders.** Flowspace intermittently ships an
-  order with an empty per-package item array even though the order has order-level
-  `lineItemsV2` and a tracked package. It is a **fulfillment-path** behavior, not a
-  contract bug: orders where the retailer dictates the carrier/label (merchant-routed
-  dropship — Amazon FBM, Target Plus, Wayfair, Home Depot, Walmart) skip per-package
-  item capture 14–25% of the time, while orders Flowspace rate-shops itself
-  (`carrier: null`) capture items 100% of the time. Recording package contents at
-  fulfillment is optional by default — hence the `packageItemsRequired` toggle (see
-  Field-mapping decisions).

-  `orderLineItemsAttributes`, but each has unmapped fields**: freight-only

-  parcel service decision below).
-  `parcelService` exists on both input types with an identical, undocumented
-  description — see the `shipping_method_id` rejection decision below for why we don't
-  forward it on freight.

-    excluded: no schema query lists rate quotes, only an opaque `selectedShippingRateId`
-    (null on all sampled orders); the chosen carrier's actual cost already maps to
-    `packages[].shipping_cost` via `transportation.costInCents`.
-  - Evidence: live freight orders on the Rowlo LLC prod connection (e.g. order
-    `3005930639`, pallet 48x40x59 @ 855 lbs). `pallets` is null on parcel orders, hence
-    the `or []`.

-    per-package item contents at fulfillment.

-    Setting it at the input level is rejected with

-    create test (order `1318593841`); the create is accepted without us sending any
-    packages/shipments.

-    future Trackstar-created orders. Luminous (the OMS) creates all of this customer's
-    orders via `POST /wms/orders`, so the directive reaches them.

+  - Evidence: Pylon #4273 (order `5609035497`, Wayfair) and #4561 (`6561807448`, Home
+    Depot EDI), both created without the flag and shipped with empty items.

-  - Decision: when an order is fully shipped (`packages and status == "fulfilled"`) but
-    aggregated `shipment_line_items` is empty, backfill it from the order `line_items`
-    (mirrors `infoplus/integration.py:format_order`). Flowspace emits one shipment per
-    fully-shipped order, so this is safe at the shipment level.

-    orders that already shipped empty, and does not cover any order created outside our

-  - Evidence: Pylon #4273, #4561 — same orders as above; verified the backfill populates

-> **Doctrine version:** 2.3 · last updated 2026-09-22 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.
+> **Doctrine version:** 2.4 · last updated 2026-09-28 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.

> Versioned **independently of the skills that consume it.** Changes to the rules below bump the doctrine version here — not `/plan-integration`'s. The skills point at this file; they don't own its history. (Pre-1.0 doctrine changes were tracked under `plan-integration` CHANGELOG entries 1.17–1.31, before the doctrine carried its own version.)

This file is the canonical pattern reference for integration subagents (`integration-api-validator`, `integration-function-writer`, `integration-reviewer`). Subagents start with clean context and **do not** auto-load the project CLAUDE.md, so this file duplicates the rules subagents need.

**Vendor variants that aren't a literal 403** still use the same shape. The trigger is "permission missing for this URL" — whether the signal is HTTP 403, HTTP 402 (payment required → billing tier doesn't include this), a JSON `errors[].message == "Access denied."` inside a 401, or text like `"AuthorizationException"` in the body. Detect the signal, then run the same record-and-raise.

+**Under the permission validator, one call per endpoint is proof of access.** Its gets run under a short time limit, so a `get_*` that walks a catalogue or makes a detail call per record branches on `self.in_perm_validator()` and requests a page size of 1: inline, no constant, no comment. A bigger "safe" page brings the timeout back as the account grows.
##### Reviewer enforcement (permission tracking)

- 403 (or vendor-equivalent permission signal) raises `create_invalid_credentials_exception` instead of `create_permissions_exception(path)` → `[BLOCK]`. The customer gets a "creds are bad" notification when the right remediation is "grant scope to this URL."

# yarn test

A wrapper around pytest with filter flags. Never run `python -m pytest` or raw `pytest`.

## Scope Arguments

Optional, can combine multiple:
```bash
yarn test integrations          # or "ints" - integration tests
yarn test api                   # Flask API tests
yarn test celery                # Celery tests
yarn test lambda                # Lambda task tests
yarn test utils                 # Utility tests
yarn test lambda utils          # Multiple scopes
```

`transports` is also a scope, and `nonints` runs every non-integration suite (api, celery, lambda, utils, transports). With no scope, everything runs in parallel.

## Integration Type Filters

Combined with OR:
```bash
--wms                           # WMS integrations only
--cart                          # Cart integrations only
--carrier                       # Carrier integrations only
--erp                           # ERP integrations only
--freight                       # Freight integrations only (legacy)
```

## Resource Filters

Each flag selects the matching `@pytest.mark.<marker>` (dashes become underscores). Resource flags OR together, across groups too. Cart uses the shared `--products`, `--orders` and `--warehouses`.

**Shared / common:**
```bash
--inventory
--products
--orders                        # WMS/cart orders
--warehouses
--locations
--returns
--customers
```

**WMS:**
```bash
--kits
--inbounds
--shipping
--bills
--labor
```

**Carrier:**
```bash
--invoices
```

```bash

## Auth shape

-- **Custom session-token header, exchanged at install.** `POST /users/sign_in` (no auth header) with `{"user":{"email","password"}}` returns `token`. -- **No refresh endpoint.** No documented TTL; "one concurrent login per account" (a browser login invalidates the API token). On 401 `clarus_request` re-signs-in once, saves the secret (when `connection_id` is set), retries. Auth calls use `ignore_log=True` (creds and token in bodies).

-- **`create_order_shipment` verifies after write.** It snapshots fulfillment ids before the POST, re-`GET`s
-  after, and raises a `400` `PokedexException` (`origin="integration"`) if no new id appeared; the message
-  names the shipped-before-created cause when `shipped_date < creationDate`. Why: the `201` is unreliable, and
-  without the check the customer got a misleading `200` with no shipment. We surface eBay's discard, we don't
-  pre-screen the request. Evidence: Pylon #4422, Datadog trace `4761577796659203049`; the 2026-05-20 re-post
-  reproduced the discard and the check raised.
-- **`create_order_shipment` formats the order re-fetched after the POST.** The pre-POST snapshot (used only for
-  SKU to `lineItemId`) has stale `status: open`, which failed the `partially_fulfilled | fulfilled` response
-  validator even on success. Evidence: Pylon #4422 `Response Validation Exception ... Got open instead`.
-- **SKU is `quote(sku, safe="")`-encoded at every `sell/inventory/v1/inventory_item/{sku}` path**
-  (`get_products`, `adjust_inventory`). Why: see the `/` and `#` quirk. Evidence: connection
-  `5238ee30...` failed every hourly `get_products` crawl with `errorId 25710` until encoded; all 4 SKUs then
-  returned `200` and the prod dry-run crawl completed with 382 items.

+  - Evidence: Pylon #4273, #4561 — same orders as above; verified the backfill populates
+    `EC700356 ×1` for `6561807448` and leaves normally-populated orders untouched.
# Integration Patterns — Operational Source of Truth
-> **Doctrine version:** 2.4 · last updated 2026-09-28 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.
+> **Doctrine version:** 2.3 · last updated 2026-09-22 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) in this directory.

> Versioned **independently of the skills that consume it.** Changes to the rules below bump the doctrine version here — not `/plan-integration`'s. The skills point at this file; they don't own its history. (Pre-1.0 doctrine changes were tracked under `plan-integration` CHANGELOG entries 1.17–1.31, before the doctrine carried its own version.)

This file is the canonical pattern reference for integration subagents (`integration-api-validator`, `integration-function-writer`, `integration-reviewer`). Subagents start with clean context and **do not** auto-load the project CLAUDE.md, so this file duplicates the rules subagents need.

**Vendor variants that aren't a literal 403** still use the same shape. The trigger is "permission missing for this URL" — whether the signal is HTTP 403, HTTP 402 (payment required → billing tier doesn't include this), a JSON `errors[].message == "Access denied."` inside a 401, or text like `"AuthorizationException"` in the body. Detect the signal, then run the same record-and-raise.

-**Under the permission validator, one call per endpoint is proof of access.** Its gets run under a short time limit, so a `get_*` that walks a catalogue or makes a detail call per record branches on `self.in_perm_validator()` and requests a page size of 1: inline, no constant, no comment. A bigger "safe" page brings the timeout back as the account grows.
##### Reviewer enforcement (permission tracking)

- 403 (or vendor-equivalent permission signal) raises `create_invalid_credentials_exception` instead of `create_permissions_exception(path)` → `[BLOCK]`. The customer gets a "creds are bad" notification when the right remediation is "grant scope to this URL."
